news.title: GTCR Reopens Global Payments Buyout Evaluation
news.body: GTCR disclosed that it is evaluating a potential Global Payments acquisition after an earlier consortium effort with CD&R ended. PYMNTS attributed an approximately $50 billion transaction estimate, including debt, to Bloomberg—not to an agreed offer. GTCR already owns approximately 16%, and any acquisition would encompass a processor integrating Worldpay after selling Issuer Solutions to FIS. GTCR has announced neither an acquisition agreement nor changes to merchant services.

news.title: TPG and Corpay Agree to Buy BILL for Approximately $6 Billion
news.body: BILL agreed to a $63.25-per-share cash acquisition valuing the business at approximately $6 billion, with TPG taking a majority interest and Corpay a minority stake. Closing is expected in the first half of 2027, subject to shareholder and regulatory approvals, with René Lacerte remaining CEO. The buyers previously agreed to acquire AvidXchange, but have announced no combination or shared product roadmap for BILL’s nearly 500,000 business customers.

news.title: Mexico Revises Proposed Card Interchange Caps
news.body: Mexico’s revised proposal would phase in annual average interchange caps of 1% for credit cards and 0.3% for debit cards by 2029, easing the earlier proposed 0.6% credit cap. The government estimates roughly 20 billion pesos in annual savings, predominantly for acquirers. Merchant savings would depend on whether acquirers pass through the reductions in their commercial pricing. The caps remain proposed rather than final requirements.

news.title: Worldline Rejects Accounting Allegations and Reiterates Cash-Flow Forecast
news.body: Following FT reporting on historical supplier-payment delays and customer cash advances, Worldline rejected allegations of accounting irregularities and reiterated its 2026 free-cash-flow forecast of negative €60 million to negative €40 million. According to PYMNTS’ account, a late-2023 PwC assessment estimated that 2022 free cash flow would have been €200 million below the reported €520 million without those practices. The reporting concerns historical cash generation; it does not establish a current settlement interruption or merchant-funds shortfall.

news.title: Stablecoin Advisory Flags January Approval Deadline
news.body: Payment-stablecoin issuers generally need approval to continue issuing after January 18, 2027, with no automatic grandfathering, according to PYMNTS. Eligible existing issuers with substantially complete OCC applications pending by that date may request up to 12 months of discretionary relief. The report distinguishes legal issuers responsible for reserves and redemption from distributors and branded front ends, so a customer-facing platform’s obligations depend on its role. Application forms were still awaiting federal clearance, the article reported.

perspective: GTCR’s Global Payments evaluation and BILL’s agreed sale lead developments spanning payments ownership, merchant fees, processor cash reporting and stablecoin approvals.

curiosity.text: The Bank of Finland launched Avant in 1993 through its subsidiary Toimiraha; commercial banks acquired the system in 1995. The original electronic purse used contact-based smart cards: offline payments updated the value stored on the chip locally, rather than waiting for a later balance update. Source: Bank of Finland, “The world’s first central bank digital currency – Avant” — https://publications.bof.fi/bitstream/handle/10024/43886/BoFER_8_2020.pdf
